Parents Evening Booking
Your Account Details
We will initially generate an account for you using the email address you have provided to the school for communications. When we do this, you will receive an email inviting you to create a password for your account.
If you have not received the message, check your junk/spam folder and ensure that you have added the junipereducation.org domain to your safe senders list.
Logging in
You can access our booking system at any time using this link:
You will be prompted to log in by entering your email address and password. If you have not yet set your password, you can request a password reset email by clicking ‘Forgot your password’. You should use the email address you have registered with the school.
Making a Booking
The child you are booking for will show in the top right-hand corner of the screen. If you have more than one child at our school, you will see a circle for each child. Simply click on the relevant circle to select the child you want to make a booking for.
Find the teacher and time you’d like to book and click to reserve the time slot. The selection will show in green with the word “RESERVED”. The time allocated for each slot will be automatically populated.
Please note: the slot will only be reserved for 10 minutes.
To confirm the reservation you’ll need to click on the save button in the bottom right corner.

pageCache.text:
St. John's School Governors
Welcome to the Governors' section.
The purpose of the governing body:
The governing body is the school’s responsible body. It operates at a strategic level with three main responsibilities:
1. Ensuring clarity of the Catholic vision, ethos and strategic direction; 2. Holding the head teacher to account for the educational performance and Catholic character of the school and its pupils; and 3. Overseeing the financial performance of the school and making sure its money is well spent
Our school's governing body is made up of 4 different categories of governors:
Foundation Governors:
There are seven Foundation Governors. Foundation Governors are practising Catholics appointed by the Bishop of the Diocese of Portsmouth.
Local Authority Governors:
There is one Local Authority Governor appointed by the Local Authority.
There are two Parent Governors who are elected by the parents of children who attend the school.
There is one staff Governor (who can be a teacher or non-teacher) who is elected by other staff.

Welcome to Nursery
We are an Ofsted Outstanding Nursery
At St. John’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School, we aim to provide a spiritual, safe and stimulating environment in our nursery, where children can develop fully at their own pace.
Play is probably the most valuable work your child will do. In their play, children learn at their highest level.
We inspire learning through excellent play opportunities and provide a varied curriculum based on children’s individual needs.
Communication and language is one of the most important parts of our early year’s curriculum. We provide a rich language environment, where children can develop their confidence and skills in expressing themselves.
Our thoughtfully planned learning opportunities aim to lead the children towards self-motivation and achievement; encourage self-discipline and perseverance and to think critically and make links with the world around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: St John's Cathedral Catholic Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At St John’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School, our curriculum is deliberately designed to be ambitious for all and to ensure that every pupil, including those who are disadvantaged or with SEND, can learn and succeed. It provides a rich, balanced and challenging education that builds systematically on prior learning so that all pupils make excellent progress. Rooted firmly in our Catholic identity, our curriculum aims to shape pupils into responsible, reflective 21st‑Century Christians who recognise their God‑given dignity and the dignity of all. Our Gospel Values—love, respect, honesty, generosity, creativity, responsibility and justice—are not simply taught but lived, forming the moral and spiritual foundation of our school. We want pupils to understand how they can make a positive contribution to their local community and wider society, developing an awareness of their role as global citizens and the challenges faced by humanity. Our mission, “Loving to Learn; Learning to Love,” underpins every aspect of curriculum. We strive to equip pupils with the knowledge, character and cultural capital they need to thrive academically, spiritually and socially.
High-quality planning and teaching at St John’s ensures that learning is ambitious for every pupil, with inclusive and adaptive classroom practice enabling all children—including those who are disadvantaged or with SEND—to secure strong foundations and access the full breadth of the curriculum. Teachers use a carefully sequenced, topic‑based approach that builds securely on prior knowledge so pupils can make strong progress over time. Creative, engaging subject teaching lies at the heart of this approach, supported by strong subject knowledge and a clear understanding of curriculum progression. Personalised support is embedded within high‑quality first teaching, complemented by evidence‑informed interventions when needed. Catholic Social Teaching continues to be woven through every subject, enabling pupils to explore big questions, engage in meaningful project work and understand how to put faith into action. Drawing on Portsmouth’s rich local history, we provide memorable experiences and purposeful trips that deepen learning across the curriculum. Our broad and strong extra‑curricular offer—including sport, music and play‑based clubs—further enriches pupils’ personal development, nurturing their gifts, confidence and wellbeing.
Through our authentic commitment to teaching and learning, the school currently holds an outstanding judgement for its Catholic Schools Inspection, is a long-standing Artsmark school and holds an Oscar Romero Award for faith in action. Our trusting partnership with parents and high expectations for all, means pupils become resilient and lifelong learners with a passion for social justice. Enjoyment of the curriculum is demonstrated through the children’s high achievements, excellent attendance, their confidence and exemplary behaviour. Our data reflects this with attainment consistently above national and local results. Pupils feel safe, loved and certainly thrive at St John’s.

pageCache.text:
Latest Newsletter (website translatable version)
Dear Parents/Carers,
Welcome back to a new school year. I hope that you had a lovely summer and are excited about the new school year ahead. We offer a special welcome to the new staff, children and families who have joined us and we pray that their time at St John’s will happy, successful and filled with blessings.
Vision and Mission Statement
We believe that a bright future starts with an excellent education.
Our vision is to ignite a love of learning that enables every child to achieve their very best. We aim to provide the excellent teaching and genuine nurture that will enable all of our children to be happy, resilient, creative citizens who have the skills, knowledge and passion to change the world.
Our mission at St John’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School is to educate the whole child through the Gospel values of Christ and provide academic excellence within a Catholic community, where all are loving to learn and learning to love.
School Improvement Plan 2025-2028
Priority 1: Curriculum and Teaching
Ensure that feedback and assessment are used highly effectively so that all children achieve exceptionally well across the curriculum.
Priority 2: Leadership and Governance
Develop and formalise comprehensive and highly effective systems for induction and health and safety
Develop the EYFS outdoor provision to address all areas of learning
Priority 4: Catholic Life/Worship/Curriculum
Ensure that policies and practices are updated to reflect the new RED and Prayer and Liturgy Directory
We welcome Mrs Hoile who is our new art teacher and we welcome Miss Kolwin who joins us as an LSA in Year 2.
We pray for Miss Minall who had an accident last week and is currently in hospital. We wish her a speedy recovery. Miss Turner will now be teaching Tuesday to Friday in Year 1 and Mrs Munns will teach on the Monday for the next couple of weeks until Miss Minall returns.
We say goodbye to Mrs Brown and Mrs Gardner who are both retiring. As you know Mrs Gardner was involved in a traumatic road traffic accident last year and received significant and life changing injuries. She is making incredible progress and showing the courage and resilience that we all know of her. However, her recovery journey is still ongoing. We wish her a long and happy retirement and send her our prayers, thanks and best wishes.
Mrs Brown has also had a difficult year with ongoing health issues which prevent her from being around large groups of people. She is also showing incredible courage and resilience in managing her illness but unfortunately is unable to return to work. We wish her a long and happy retirement and send her our prayers, thanks and best wishes too.
Both Mrs Brown and Mrs Gardner have worked at St John’s for a very long time and have been invaluable in developing our school as a community that loves to learn and learns to love. If you wish to donate to their retirement collection, please drop your donations in to the office in an envelope marked ‘Mrs Brown collection’ and/or ’Mrs Gardner collection.’
If you have any safeguarding concerns, please note that the school’s DSL (designated safeguarding lead) is me, Mrs Park and the DDSL (deputy designated safeguarding lead) is Mrs Warren.
If your child is having a school dinner, please ensure that you have ordered on scopay. The kitchen is only able to cook and provide lunches for those who have booked in advance. If a child has not ordered a school dinner and does not have a packed lunch with them, we will phone the contacts on Arbor for a meal to be dropped into school.
Thank you for sending your children back to school in their full school uniform. They look incredibly smart and proud. Children are able to wear summer or winter uniform until October half term when they will need to move to winter uniform. Please continue to support us by adhering to the uniform policy. As the weather has started to change, please ensure that your child always has a coat with them too.

Hair longer than shoulder length must be tied back.
Hair should be no shorter than grade 1 and without shaven designs.
Dyed hair, coloured braids or extreme styles are not permitted.
Any hair accessories should be hair coloured or uniform coloured
No necklaces, bracelets or smart watches are to be worn and if earrings are worn they need to be studs.
Mobile phones and smart watches
Children who bring mobile phones or smart watches to school must drop them into the office before they go onto the playground in the morning. At the end of the day, they need to leave the playground and walk around to the office to collect them.
Parents and visitors are not permitted to use mobile phones in school. They should be switched off and put away if you enter the building. There may be occasions such as school events when a member of staff will permit photographs but we will share our expectations at the time.
Medicines and medical conditions
If your child has a medical condition, including any allergies, please ensure that the school office are aware.
The office are able to administer prescribed medicines that are needed during the school day and that can’t be administered at home eg inhalers, 4x day antibiotics where 3 doses are given at home and 1 is needed at lunchtime. The medicines must be prescribed, have the child’s name and dose on and be in the original packaging. They should be handed directly to the office and not left in the school bag or handed to the class teacher and a permission slip completed.
School Nurse drop in clinic 15th October 2026
Appointments can be made at the school office.
Prayer, scripture and play club and choir
A communication will be sent out in the coming weeks with the starting date and arrangements for these 2 clubs.
Next Sunday, 13th September, is Education Sunday. St John’s is celebrating this at the 12 O’clock Mass at the cathedral. We invite all our families to attend and children to wear their school uniform. We invite our new Reception children to process in at the beginning of Mass and many of our children will be involved in the various ministries. Please bring you child along for this important celebration of Catholic education.
I have received a letter from Bishop Philip announcing that the cathedral is launching a new cathedral choir for boys and girls aged 8-14. This is a very exciting opportunity and with the talent and enthusiasm that our children show for music, I’m sure many of our children will be keen to sign up. If your child would like to find out more, please collect a letter from the office with the contact details.
School Building Fund
As you will be aware, as a Catholic school, St John’s is voluntary aided and is only partly funded by the state. We receive only 90% of the allocated capital funding each year. To cover the remaining 10%, Catholic schools must ask all parents/carers to make a contribution through the school building fund to pay for the necessary building and repair projects. Generations of parents/carers have made this contribution in the past so that we have the school that we are so proud of today.
Thank you to those who have already paid and I ask those who haven’t to please consider making the contribution as soon as possible.
We are delighted to have a new nursery garden for our youngest children to explore, learn and play in.
As always, thank you so much for your support and generosity in making St John’s the wonderful place that is and helping us to live out our mission of Learning to Love and Loving to Learn.
